title_en: Hot Off The Assembly Line: Alaska Airlines Takes Delivery Of 6th Boeing 787-9 Dreamliner
title_zh: 热线下线：阿拉斯加航空接收第六架波音 787-9 梦想客机
summary: Alaska Airlines welcomes its sixth Boeing 787-9 as further Dreamliner deliveries promise new routes and upgraded premium cabins.
summary_zh: 阿拉斯加航空迎来第六架波音 787-9，更多梦想飞机交付有望开辟新航线并升级高级客舱。
body_en: Hot Off The Assembly Line: Alaska Airlines Takes Delivery Of 6th Boeing 787-9 Dreamliner

Paul has had a career of 25+ years focused on the international technology sector, which has taken him to over 100 countries. Along the way, he developed a deep love for aviation, with a travel bucket list measured by aircraft types flown rather than destinations reached. Now he brings that avgeek passion, along with the journalism experience he accumulated early in his career, to write insightful pieces for Simple Flying.

Alaska Airlines has welcomed its sixth 787-9 Dreamliner , with the aircraft departing Boeing's Charleston, South Carolina, facility earlier this morning, bound for Los Angeles. The aircraft, identified as N785HA, marks another milestone in the carrier's ambitious long-haul expansion, which has accelerated considerably since it acquired Hawaiian Airlines .

The latest arrival brings Alaska's 787 fleet to six aircraft, with another 11 on order. The airline is preparing to launch additional European services in 2027, while its longer-term plans call for an expanding international network supported by both the 787-9 and the larger 787-10 .

The newest aircraft is a factory-fresh 787-9, manufacturer serial number 66469 and Boeing line number 1340. The aircraft, which has been doing test and acceptance flights for the past few weeks, departed Charleston at 11:46 AM local time for a nearly five-hour flight to Los Angeles International Airport (LAX), according to Flightradar24 . There, the aircraft will undergo initial ramp checks, hardware customization, and staging before being repositioned north to Alaska's hub at Seattle-Tacoma International Airport (SEA).

The aircraft wears Alaska's distinctive Aurora global livery , introduced as part of its international transformation. The airline describes the design as inspired by the northern lights, reflecting both its heritage and its ambitions as a global carrier.
Alaska CEO Ben Minicucci recently spoke about the carrier's Dreamliner investment.

"These planes will fuel our expansion to more destinations across the globe and ensure our guests travel aboard the newest, most fuel-efficient and state-of-the-art aircraft. We are also incredibly proud to be partnering with Boeing, a Pacific Northwest neighbor and a company that stands as a symbol of American innovation and manufacturing.”

The new Dreamliner retains the original 300-seat configuration inherited from Hawaiian Airlines , comprising 34 lie-flat business-class suites, 79 Extra Comfort seats, and 187 economy seats. Hawaiian received its first 787-9 in February 2024, before Alaska Air Group completed its acquisition that September. Since then, the Dreamliners have become central to Alaska's international expansion, with the newest aircraft joining a fleet serving destinations across Europe and Asia.
11 More Boeing 787-9 Dreamliners Are On Order

Alaska's record-breaking January 2026 aircraft order included five additional Dreamliners, exercising its remaining options and increasing its firm fleet commitment to 17 aircraft. With the sixth now delivered, 11 remain outstanding. The order will introduce the larger 787-10 alongside the existing 787-9 fleet, providing more capacity for the airline's expanding international operation.

Deliveries will accelerate from 2028. Speaking to Airliner World earlier this month, Alaska's SVP of Fleet, Shane Jones, confirmed that aircraft number seven is expected in 2027, followed by four in 2028. Alaska's regulatory fleet forecast identifies all four 2028 deliveries as 787-10s, with the remaining aircraft deliveries yet to be determined, but expected by 2032.

The new aircraft will also support Alaska's premium-cabin transformation. Beginning in late 2027, the airline plans to retrofit its existing Dreamliners with Aurora Suites and Premium Reserve seating. Updated 787-9s will feature 34 business-class suites, while the 787-10s will offer 40. Alaska ultimately expects premium seating to account for approximately 46% of its refurbished 787-9s, compared with 38% today.

Alaska currently operates Dreamliners from Seattle to Tokyo Narita Airport (NRT), Seoul's Incheon International Airport (ICN), London Heathrow Airport (LHR) and Rome Fiumicino Airport (FCO), with the latter operating seasonally. Two more European destinations will join in May 2027: Athens, launching May 12, and Paris, beginning May 25. Athens will become Alaska's longest route, at approximately 6,150 miles (9,897 km), with both services operating through October.

At its September Investor Day , Alaska outlined plans to grow its intercontinental network to 10 destinations by 2028 and 15 by 2030, although some will use aircraft other than Dreamliners. Management indicated that another Asian destination was under development but did not identify the city. The Investor Day presentation also explicitly linked network expansion to the arrival of additional widebody aircraft.

Several potential destinations stand out. Ho Chi Minh City has been repeatedly linked to Alaska's ambitions through earlier executive comments about serving Vietnam, while Bangkok has also emerged as a possibility. Neither has nonstop flights from Seattle today. Sydney would represent a significant move into the Australian market, while Madrid could expand Alaska's European network and offer onward connections through oneworld partner Iberia .

None of these routes has been announced yet, and Alaska will also need to strike a balance between optimal range and capacity planning as it moves to operating two Dreamliner variants. With 11 additional Dreamliners coming, today's delivery marks another step toward Alaska Airlines' substantially larger global network.
body_zh: 热线下线：阿拉斯加航空接收第六架波音 787-9 梦想客机
Paul 拥有超过 25 年的职业生涯，专注于国际技术领域，足迹遍布 100 多个国家。一路走来，他对航空产生了深深的热爱，他的旅行愿望清单是根据飞行的飞机类型而不是到达的目的地来衡量的。现在，他带着这种狂热的热情，以及他在职业生涯早期积累的新闻经验，为《简单的飞行》撰写了富有洞察力的文章。
阿拉斯加航空迎来了第六架 787-9 梦想客机，这架飞机于今天上午早些时候从波音公司位于南卡罗来纳州查尔斯顿的工厂出发，飞往洛杉矶。这架编号为 N785HA 的飞机标志着该航空公司雄心勃勃的长途扩张计划的又一个里程碑，自收购夏威夷航空以来，该计划已大大加速。
最新抵达的这架飞机使阿拉斯加的 787 机队数量达到 6 架，另外还订购了 11 架。该航空公司正准备在 2027 年推出更多欧洲航班，而其长期计划则要求扩大由 787-9 和更大的 787-10 飞机支持的国际网络。
最新的飞机是一架刚出厂的 787-9，制造商序列号为 66469，波音系列号为 1340。据 Flightradar24 报道，这架飞机过去几周一直在进行测试和验收飞行，于当地时间上午 11 点 46 分从查尔斯顿起飞，经过近 5 个小时的飞行抵达洛杉矶国际机场 (LAX)。在那里，飞机将接受初步的坡道检查、硬件定制和升级，然后重新定位到阿拉斯加北部的西雅图-塔科马国际机场 (SEA) 枢纽。
该飞机拥有阿拉斯加独特的极光全球涂装，这是其国际化转型的一部分。该航空公司称其设计灵感来自北极光，反映了其传统和作为全球航空公司的雄心。
阿拉斯加航空公司首席执行官本·米尼库奇 (Ben Minicucci) 最近谈到了该航空公司对梦想飞机的投资。
“这些飞机将推动我们向全球更多目的地的扩张，并确保我们的客人乘坐最新、最省油且最先进的飞机。我们也非常自豪能够与太平洋西北邻国波音公司合作，该公司是美国创新和制造的象征。”
全新梦想飞机保留了夏威夷航空原有的300个座位配置，包括34个平躺式商务舱套房、79个Extra Comfort座位和187​​个经济舱座位。夏威夷航空于 2024 年 2 月接收了第一架 787-9，随后阿拉斯加航空集团于当年 9 月完成了收购。从那时起，梦想飞机已成为阿拉斯加国际扩张的核心，最新的飞机加入了服务欧洲和亚洲目的地的机队。
另有 11 架波音 787-9 梦想飞机正在订购中
阿拉斯加航空 2026 年 1 月破纪录的飞机订单包括另外 5 架梦想飞机，行使其剩余选择权并将其坚定的机队承诺增加到 17 架飞机。目前已交付第六架，还有 11 架尚未交付。该订单将在现有 787-9 机队的同时引入更大的 787-10，为该航空公司不断扩大的国际运营提供更多运力。
从 2028 年开始，交付量将加速。本月早些时候，阿拉斯加机队高级副总裁肖恩·琼斯 (Shane Jones) 在接受《航空世界》采访时证实，预计 2027 年将交付 7 架飞机，随后在 2028 年将交付 4 架飞机。阿拉斯加的监管机队预测将 2028 年交付的所有四架飞机均为 787-10，其余飞机交付量尚未确定，但预计将在 2032 年交付。
新飞机还将支持阿拉斯加的高级客舱转型。从 2027 年底开始，该航空公司计划对其现有的梦想飞机进行改造，配备极光套房和高级预留座位。更新后的 787-9 飞机将配备 34 间商务舱套房，而 787-10 飞机将提供 40 间商务舱套房。阿拉斯加最终预计高级座位数将占其翻新 787-9 飞机的约 46%，而目前这一比例为 38%。
阿拉斯加目前运营从西雅图飞往东京成田机场 (NRT)、首尔仁川国际机场 (ICN)、伦敦希思罗机场 (LHR) 和罗马菲乌米奇诺机场 (FCO) 的梦想飞机，后者季节性运营。另外两个欧洲目的地将于 2027 年 5 月加入：雅典（5 月 12 日开通）和巴黎（5 月 25 日开始）。雅典将成为阿拉斯加最长的航线，全长约 6,150 英里（9,897 公里），两条航线均运营至 10 月。
在 9 月份的投资者日上，阿拉斯加概述了计划到 2028 年将其洲际网络扩大到 10 个目的地，到 2030 年扩大到 15 个目的地，尽管其中一些目的地将使用梦想飞机以外的飞机。管理层表示另一个亚洲目的地正在开发中，但没有透露具体城市。投资者日演讲还明确将网络扩张与更多宽体飞机的到来联系起来。
几个潜在的目的地脱颖而出。通过早些时候有关为越南服务的高管评论，胡志明市已多次与阿拉斯加的雄心联系在一起，而曼谷也成为了一种可能性。今天两者都没有从西雅图出发的直飞航班。悉尼将代表着进军澳大利亚市场的重大举措，而马德里则可以扩大阿拉斯加的欧洲网络，并通过寰宇一家合作伙伴伊比利亚航空提供转程航班。
这些航线尚未公布，阿拉斯加在运营两架梦想飞机时还需要在最佳航程和运力规划之间取得平衡。随着另外 11 架梦想飞机的到来，今天的交付标志着阿拉斯加航空朝着更大的全球网络又迈出了一步。

title_en: Ouch: United Launches “Basic” Domestic First Class Fares, And They’re Restrictive
title_zh: 哎哟：美联航推出“基本”国内头等舱票价，而且有限制
summary: United has started selling basic domestic first class fares that are non-refundable, charge $199 for changes, skip free seat selection, and earn no redeemable miles. Here's what changed.
summary_zh: 美联航已开始销售不可退款的基本国内头等舱票价，改签收费 199 美元，跳过免费选座，并且不赚取任何退款
body_en: At this point, just about all passengers are familiar with the concept of “basic economy,” whereby the cheapest economy tickets in many markets come with a lot of restrictions, in an effort to get people to buy-up to more expensive fares. In recent times, we’ve increasingly seen that also spread to premium cabins.
This spring, United Airlines introduced a basic product for its Polaris business class , and now the airline has rolled out a “basic” product for its domestic first class.
Details of United’s restrictive new first class fares
As of October 28, 2026, United has started selling “basic” fares in domestic first class, as flagged by Live and Let’s Fly . You’ll now find this available in many markets.
When you start your search, you’ll see a box you can check that says “Include Basic economy & restrictive fares.”
Then when you see fares in a particular domestic market, you’ll see the “United Economy” and “United First” columns.

When you click on the first class option, you’ll now see up to three fare types — Base, Standard, and Flexible. Essentially what’s changing is that the most basic fares are non-refundable, changes cost $199, they don’t allow complimentary seat selections, and they also don’t earn any redeemable miles (though they do earn Premier Qualifying Points, based on the amount spent).

Broadly speaking, it would appear that in some cases the Base fare is a little cheaper than the previous cheapest fare, but the Standard fare (which gets you the same perks as the old cheapest fare) is now more expensive. After all, the goal here is to increase revenue.

In recent years, we’ve seen first class generally become much more reasonably priced, as airlines have increasingly tried to monetize the cabin, rather than primarily fill seats with those upgrading. So there’s no denying that this will represent a pretty significant fare hike, at least for those who value the basic flexibility and perks they’ve come to expect when booking these tickets. Essentially having to pay $75 to avoid restrictions is less than ideal.
Airline executives have funny “basic” fare justifications
Don’t get me wrong, basic fares make a lot of sense from the perspective of airlines, in terms of being able to segment customers, and get people to pay as much as they’re willing to pay.

What’s funny is that no matter how popular the basic fare is, airline executives will always take a victory lap about the concept. If a lot of people book the basic fares, they’ll brag about how successful they are. If few people book the basic fares, they’ll brag about how willing people are to buy the more expensive fares.

For example, during the Q3 2026 earnings call, United Chief Commercial Officer Andrew Nocella was asked about the new tiered fare categories, particularly the “basic” business class concept, and how they’re doing with that. I thought Nocella’s answer was interesting

I will say that we are really pleased by the launch of the tiered products, and we are doing a bit more in the next few weeks. I think it has been great for our customers. It provides more options for them. And great for the airline as well. We redesigned united.com specifically to sell them effectively, and we will continue to refine our approach on that I think has even more upside. The buy up rates are incredibly high. Consumers know what they are buying, and we disclose it very carefully. This has worked for years. It started with basic economy, a little more than 10 years ago.
So Nocella thinks that the introduction of basic business class has been great for both customers and the airline, while noting that buy up rates have been incredibly high.

If buy up rates are incredibly high, then it absolutely is good for the airline (assuming minimal business has been lost), but how exactly is that good for customers? They’re paying more to get the same thing that they previously had included?

United Airlines has rolled out basic first class fares on domestic flights, following a similar rollout on international business class flights earlier in the year. With this, the cheapest first class fares no longer allow free seat assignments or changes, and they also don’t earn any redeemable miles.

Airlines of course do everything they can to segment customers, which makes sense, from their perspective. However, that doesn’t mean we have to like these changes, because it ultimately amounts to a price hike.
What do you make of United’s new basic domestic first class fares?
body_zh: 目前，几乎所有乘客都熟悉“基础经济舱”的概念，即许多市场上最便宜的经济舱机票都带有很多限制，以吸引人们购买更昂贵的票价。最近，我们越来越多地看到这种情况也蔓延到高级客舱。
今年春天，美联航推出了北极星商务舱的基础产品，现在该公司又推出了国内头等舱的“基础”产品。
美联航限制性新头等舱票价的详细信息
截至2026年10月28日，美联航已开始销售国内头等舱的“基本”票价，如Live和Let's Fly所标记的那样。您现在可以在许多市场找到此功能。
当您开始搜索时，您会看到一个可以选中的框，其中显示“包括基本经济舱和限制性票价”。
然后，当您查看特定国内市场的票价时，您将看到“美联航经济舱”和“美联航头等舱”列。
当您单击头等舱选项时，您现在将看到最多三种票价类型 - 基本票价、标准票价和灵活票价。本质上发生的变化是，最基本的票价不可退款，改签费用为 199 美元，不允许免费选座，而且也不能赚取任何可兑换里程（尽管他们确实可以根据消费金额赚取贵宾资格积分）。
一般来说，在某些情况下，基本票价似乎比以前最便宜的票价便宜一点，但标准票价（为您提供与以前最便宜的票价相同的福利）现在更贵。毕竟，这里的目标是增加收入。
近年来，我们看到头等舱的价格普遍变得更加合理，因为航空公司越来越多地尝试将客舱货币化，而不是主要通过升级来填补座位。因此，不可否认，这将意味着票价的大幅上涨，至少对于那些看重预订这些机票时所期望的基本灵活性和福利的人来说是这样。本质上必须支付 75 美元才能避免限制并不理想。
航空公司高管有有趣的“基本”票价理由
不要误会我的意思，从航空公司的角度来看，基本票价非常有意义，因为它能够对客户进行细分，并让人们支付他们愿意支付的费用。
有趣的是，无论基本票价多么受欢迎，航空公司高管总是会为这个概念欢呼雀跃。如果很多人预订基本票价，他们就会吹嘘自己有多成功。如果很少有人预订基本票价，他们就会吹嘘人们多么愿意购买更昂贵的票价。
例如，在 2026 年第三季度财报电话会议上，美联航首席商务官安德鲁·诺塞拉 (Andrew Nocella) 被问及新的分级票价类别，特别是“基本”商务舱概念，以及他们如何利用这一概念。我觉得诺塞拉的回答很有趣

我想说的是，我们对分层产品的推出感到非常高兴，并且我们将在接下来的几周内做更多的事情。我认为这对我们的客户来说非常棒。它为他们提供了更多的选择。对于航空公司来说也很棒。我们专门重新设计了 United.com，以便有效地销售它们，我们将继续完善我们的方法，我认为这有更多的好处。购买率高得令人难以置信。消费者知道他们在买什么，我们也非常仔细地披露这一点。这已经有效多年了。它是从十多年前的基础经济开始的。
因此，诺切拉认为基本商务舱的推出对乘客和航空公司来说都是好事，同时指出购买率非常高。
如果购买率高得令人难以置信，那么这对航空公司来说绝对是件好事（假设业务损失极小），但是这对客户到底有什么好处呢？他们花更多的钱来获得与之前包含的相同的东西？
继今年早些时候在国际商务舱航班上推出类似的票价后，联合航空在国内航班上推出了基本的头等舱票价。这样，最便宜的头等舱票价不再允许免费分配或更改座位，而且也无法赚取任何可兑换里程。
航空公司当然会尽一切努力来细分客户，从他们的角度来看，这是有道理的。然而，这并不意味着我们必须喜欢这些变化，因为它最终相当于价格上涨。

title_en: Why This Airline Gives Pilots At Least 3 Horizontal Hours Of Sleep On Its Longest Flights
title_zh: 为什么这家航空公司在其最长的航班上为飞行员提供至少 3 小时的水平睡眠
summary: Singapore Airlines' longest flights rely on hidden crew bunks and carefully planned rest periods to keep pilots and cabin crew alert.
summary_zh: 新加坡航空最长的航班依靠隐藏的机组人员铺位和精心规划的休息时间来保持飞行员和机组人员的警惕。
body_en: Why This Airline Gives Pilots At Least 3 Horizontal Hours Of Sleep On Its Longest Flights

Passionate about promoting aviation, the beauty of flight and the science behind it, Antonio is an avid reader of aviation magazines and books, and he loves visiting airshows all over the world, taking photos and writing about airplanes and helicopters as well. He is currently based in Palermo, Sicily.

One of the most surprising things about a Singapore Airlines ultra- long-haul flight is not something passengers can see. A second shift of crew is asleep above their heads while the cabin carries on as if nothing has changed. Trays are cleared, lights are dimmed, and somewhere behind a curtain, a person responsible for your safety is deliberately relaxing for work! The airline does not leave that to chance, either: its pilots are guaranteed at least three hours of sleep lying fully flat.

That promise raises a question every nervous flyer eventually asks: who is actually in charge while the people in charge are asleep? The answer involves four pilots, 13 cabin crew, a hidden staircase, and a rulebook that treats rest like fuel. Stay with it, because the most surprising part is not the beds. It is the rule that decides how long each person can stay in them.
Why Does One Flight Need Four Pilots And 13 Cabin Crew?

The short answer is arithmetic. A typical international flight carries two pilots and eight or nine flight attendants, but Singapore Airlines' SQ24 to John F. Kennedy International Airport (JFK) carries four pilots, two captains and two first officers , plus 13 cabin crew including the purser. That is four or five more flight attendants than a typical international flight, as reported by Cabincrew24 . The cabin crew total can reach 14 on some sectors, including flights to Los Angeles, according to The Sydney Morning Herald . Either way, the headcount is only the visible part of the plan. The New York route covers roughly 9,537 miles (15,349 kilometers) and can take up to 19 hours and 15 minutes in the air, far beyond what a single set of pilots may fly under duty-time rules.

Singapore Airlines has been here before, and it did not end well. The airline flew from Singapore Changi Airport to JFK from 2004 to 2013 with the four-engine Airbus A340-500 , which burned about 25% more fuel per seat than today's aircraft, and the route was paused when fuel prices rose, per Cabincrew24 . It returned in 2018 on the more fuel-efficient Airbus A350-900ULR , which carries about 43,600 gallons (165,000 liters) of fuel, roughly 6,300 gallons (24,000 liters) more than a standard Airbus A350-900 . As we previously explained , efficient new-generation widebodies like the A350 changed what airlines could risk commercially on ultra-long missions. The airline took delivery of the first one on September 22, 2018, according to Singapore Airlines' own announcement .

So the fuel problem was solved, and the economics suddenly worked better. But a jet that can stay airborne for 19 hours is useless if the people operating it cannot. Which leaves a stranger puzzle: on an aircraft where every pound is counted, where does a second shift of pilots and flight attendants actually lie down?

Out of sight, and not in a passenger seat. According to Cabincrew24 , the flight attendant rest area sits toward the back of the cabin, reached by a small staircase near the fourth set of exit doors, with eight bunks behind privacy curtains, closer to a small sleeper cabin on a train than to anything in a normal cabin. Pilots get a separate compartment above the forward business class cabin with two beds and an armchair, as noted by The Smart Local in its roundup of airline secrets. If you have ever noticed the ceiling dip lower over one part of business class on a long-haul jet, you were probably looking at someone's bedroom.

Space on this aircraft is a precious commodity. As detailed in Singapore Airlines' announcement of the cabin layout , the A350-900ULR is restricted to 161 seats, 67 in business class and 94 in premium economy , with no economy or first class , because a standard economy class on such a long flight cannot be tolerated well by passengers, and weight has to be traded for fuel. Against that backdrop, the bunks are a deliberate exception. The airline chose to spend weight on sleep rather than revenue, which shows how seriously it takes rested crew. Every bunk displaces something that could have earned money, and Singapore Airlines decided that was a fair trade.
Eight bunks for 13 flight attendants and two beds for four pilots. The math only works if nobody sleeps at the same time. So how long does each person actually get, and who decided on that number?
How Many Hours Of Sleep Does Each Crew Member Get?

Pilots receive at least two rest periods during the flight , one of them lasting about four hours or more, and at least three of those hours must be spent horizontal, according to The Sydney Morning Herald and Channel NewsAsia's explainer on pilot fatigue safeguards . Cabin crew receive roughly four to five hours of rest, depending on total duty time. A four-hour block is roughly a fifth of a 19-hour flight, so every minute counts. Those hours are not a courtesy. They are the plan, written into the roster before the aircraft ever leaves the gate.

The horizontal requirement is the detail worth lingering on. NASA research found that onboard bunk rest during long-haul flights helped improve flight crews’ subsequent alertness and performance, supporting the use of dedicated sleeping facilities to manage fatigue. That matters because, as described by Frontiers in Environmental Health , these routes exceed 16 hours of flight time and can stretch to 22 hours of total duty. The same research summary describes scheduled in-flight rest in lie-flat bunks as the main tool for managing fatigue on these flights. In other words, the bed is the safety equipment.

Four hours may seem modest on a duty day that can approach 24 hours, but the timing of each rest period matters. The crew cannot all disappear into the bunks at once, and some phases of the flight leave no room for anyone to rest. So how does Singapore Airlines keep the cabin running when part of the crew is asleep?
Emergency squawks, holds, NOTAMs — live signals, no signup.
Who Serves The Meals While Half The Crew Is Asleep?

Everyone, at first. According to Cabincrew24 , every crew member works the first meal service after takeoff. Once it ends, about half the cabin crew head to the bunks while the rest keep working, and the groups swap every two to three hours so a fresh team is always on the floor. The design is deliberate: the cabin never runs short-handed, and nobody goes through the whole flight without a real chance to sleep. Then everyone returns for the final service and stays seated for landing.
body_zh: 为什么这家航空公司在其最长的航班上为飞行员提供至少 3 小时的水平睡眠
安东尼奥热衷于推广航空、飞行之美及其背后的科学，是航空杂志和书籍的狂热读者，他喜欢参观世界各地的航展，也喜欢拍摄有关飞机和直升机的照片和撰写有关飞机和直升机的文章。他目前居住在西西里岛巴勒莫。
新加坡航空超长途航班最令人惊讶的事情之一就是乘客看不到的东西。第二班的船员在头顶上睡着了，而机舱继续运转，仿佛一切都没有改变。托盘被清理，灯光变暗，在窗帘后面的某个地方，负责您安全的人正在刻意放松工作！该航空公司也不会对此置之不理：保证飞行员至少可以完全平躺三个小时的睡眠。
这一承诺引发了每个紧张的乘客最终都会问的一个问题：当负责人睡着时，谁才是真正的负责人？答案涉及四名飞行员、13 名机组人员、一个隐藏的楼梯和一本将休息视为燃料的规则手册。坚持下去，因为最令人惊讶的部分不是床。规则决定了每个人可以在里面呆多久。
为什么一架航班需要 4 名飞行员和 13 名机组人员？

简短的答案是算术。典型的国际航班载有两名飞行员和八九名空乘人员，但新加坡航空飞往约翰·肯尼迪国际机场 (JFK) 的 SQ24 载有四名飞行员、两名机长和两名副驾驶，以及包括乘务长在内的 13 名机组人员。据 Cabincrew24 报道，这比典型的国际航班多了四到五名空乘人员。据《悉尼先驱晨报》报道，部分航段的机组人员总数可达 14 人，其中包括飞往洛杉矶的航班。不管怎样，人数只是计划的可见部分。纽约航线全长约 9,537 英里（15,349 公里），飞行时间可能长达 19 小时 15 分钟，远远超出了一组飞行员根据执勤时间规则飞行的时间。

新加坡航空以前也来过，但结局并不好。据 Cabincrew24 报道，从 2004 年到 2013 年，该航空公司使用四引擎空客 A340-500 执飞从新加坡樟宜机场飞往肯尼迪国际机场的航班，每座飞机的燃油消耗量比现在的飞机高出约 25%，并且该航线因燃油价格上涨而暂停。它于 2018 年回归，搭载燃油效率更高的空客 A350-900ULR，该机型可携带约 43,600 加仑（165,000 升）燃油，比标准空客 A350-900 多约 6,300 加仑（24,000 升）。正如我们之前所解释的，像 A350 这样的高效新一代宽体飞机改变了航空公司在超长任务中可能面临的商业风险。根据新加坡航空自己的公告，该航空公司于 2018 年 9 月 22 日接收了第一架飞机。
这样，燃料问题就解决了，经济效益突然好转了。但是，如果操作者不能在空中停留 19 个小时，一架喷气式飞机就毫无用处。这就留下了一个奇怪的谜题：在一架每一磅都被计算在内的飞机上，第二班的飞行员和空乘人员实际上躺在哪里？

在视线之外，也不在乘客座位上。据 Cabincrew24 报道，空乘人员休息区位于客舱后部，可通过第四组出口门附近的小楼梯到达，隐私窗帘后面有八个铺位，比普通客舱中的任何东西都更接近火车上的小型卧铺舱。正如《Smart Local》在其航空机密综述中指出的那样，飞行员在前商务舱上方有一个单独的隔间，里面有两张床和一张扶手椅。如果您曾经注意到一架长途飞机商务舱的天花板较低，那么您可能正在看某人的卧室。

这架飞机上的空间是宝贵的商品。新航公布的客舱布局公告中详细介绍，A350-900ULR的座位数被限制在161个，其中商务舱67个，豪华经济舱94个，没有经济舱和头等舱，因为这么长的航班乘坐标准经济舱乘客不太能忍受，而且必须用重量来换取燃油。在这种背景下，铺位是一个特意的例外。该航空公司选择将重点放在睡眠而不是收入上，这表明它对休息的机组人员有多么重视。每张铺位都会取代原本可以赚钱的东西，新加坡航空认为这是一项公平交易。
八个铺位可容纳 13 名空乘人员，两张床可容纳 4 名飞行员。只有当没有人同时睡觉时，数学才有效。那么每个人实际上能得到多长时间，这个数字又是谁决定的呢？
每个船员有多少小时的睡眠时间？
据《悉尼先驱晨报》和亚洲新闻台关于飞行员疲劳保障措施的解说员介绍，飞行员在飞行过程中至少有两次休息时间，其中一次持续约四个小时或更长时间，其中至少三个小时必须水平休息。机组人员大约有四到五个小时的休息时间，具体取决于总工作时间。四个小时的飞行时间大约相当于 19 小时飞行的五分之一，因此每一分钟都很重要。那些时间不是礼貌。它们就是计划，在飞机离开登机口之前就被写入名册中。
横向的要求是值得留恋的细节。美国宇航局的研究发现，长途飞行期间机上铺位休息有助于提高机组人员随后的警觉性和表现，支持使用专用睡眠设施来管理疲劳。这很重要，因为正如《环境健康前沿》所描述的那样，这些航线的飞行时间超过 16 小时，总执勤时间可能长达 22 小时。该研究摘要描述了在平躺式铺位上安排的飞行中休息是管理这些航班疲劳的主要工具。换句话说，床就是安全设备。
对于接近 24 小时的工作日来说，四个小时似乎不算多，但每个休息时间的时间安排很重要。机组人员不可能立即全部消失在铺位上，而且飞行的某些阶段没有给任何人留下休息的空间。那么，当部分机组人员睡觉时，新加坡航空如何保持机舱运行呢？
紧急呼叫、等待、航行通告 — 实时信号，无需注册。
当一半的船员都在睡觉时，谁来提供膳食？
大家一开始。据 Cabincrew24 报道，每位机组人员都会在起飞后进行第一顿餐饮服务。比赛结束后，大约一半的机组人员会前往铺位休息，而其余的机组人员则继续工作，并且每两到三个小时就会交换一次，以便始终有一个新的团队在工作。设计是经过深思熟虑的：机舱永远不会缺人，而且在整个飞行过程中，每个人都没有真正的睡觉机会。然后，每个人都返回参加最后一次服务，并留在座位上等待着陆。

title_en: Split The Cost: How Flying Clubs & Partnerships Are Making Aircraft Ownership Affordable
title_zh: 分摊成本：飞行俱乐部和合作伙伴如何使飞机所有权变得负担得起
summary: The collective owner models that make flying accessible to every aspiring aviator.
summary_zh: 集体所有者模型让每一位有抱负的飞行员都能享受飞行。
body_en: Split The Cost: How Flying Clubs & Partnerships Are Making Aircraft Ownership Affordable

Luke Diaz is a freelance military writer with experience with active duty experience in the US Navy as well as defense and industrial engineering. He is a former Naval Flight Officer who performed tactical air control on the carrier-based E-2 Hawkeye.

For anyone looking to get into general aviation, the financial aspect is typically one of the first barriers to entry. Depending on how much flying time pilots plan on flying in a year, sole ownership or direct rentals are far from the only avenue to get in the air. A casual aviator looking to spend 50 hours or less in the cockpit per year is typically best served by joining a flying club. If someone is aiming for 50 to 100 hours annually, a partnership with other flyers can offer an excellent option.

Fixed costs like hangar rent, insurance, and annual inspections remain constant regardless of how much the aircraft flies. These expenses heavily penalize pilots who let an airplane sit idle. Consequently, shared models become far more attractive at lower hour thresholds, while solo ownership only begins to make sense for highly active flyers. Club members pay a modest monthly fee and an hourly rate only when the aircraft is actually running.

As utilization climbs into the 50 to 100-hour range, the per-hour cost of a four-way partnership often beats flying clubs. Some low-cost flying clubs might still look cheaper on paper at 70 or 80 hours; a partnership eliminates the frustration of competing with dozens of club members for weekend bookings. Meanwhile, solo ownership remains difficult to justify even at 100 hours.

Sole aircraft ownership is significantly burdened with fixed expenses, resulting in a significant penalty for pilots who fly sparingly. Co-ownership models eliminate this financial bottleneck by changing how these initial expenses are shared. Flying clubs distribute these fixed liabilities across dozens of members through monthly dues and low hourly rates, while small partnerships divide the costs equally.

Financial estimates for a typical $100,000 Cessna 172 show annual fixed costs of $16,000 for hangar leasing, mandated annual inspections, Garmin navigation database subscriptions, and engine overhaul escrow. When the owner adds $1,700 for hull insurance and $2,000 for annual depreciation, he confronts thousands in fixed obligations before factoring in the $100 required for every hour of engine operation.
Emergency squawks, holds, NOTAMs — live signals, no signup.

The inefficiency of solo ownership at low usage rates is not improved when these fixed bills are amortized over the entire flying period. The actual operational cost of flying 25 hours a year is about $900 per hour. That decreases to $500 at 50 hours and to a more affordable $300 at 100 hours. Keeping a plane grounded provides no relief from the basic financial requirements of ownership, and bills will still come in even if the plane never takes off.

Clubs generally use pricing structures with set monthly dues and variable hourly fees. Monthly dues are intended to cover regular fixed expenses such as hangar space, insurance, and annual mechanical inspections. The hourly rate pays for operational costs like fuel. Because these clubs follow Federal Aviation Administration Part 91 regulations, they are non-profit private organizations for members only and cannot lawfully sell flights to the general public.

Members of equity clubs must pay a buy-in cost of between $5,000 and over $30,000 in addition to $100 to $300 in monthly dues in order to acquire an actual ownership share. Non-equity clubs, on the other hand, have lower initiation fees, with caps around $2,000, but higher monthly dues to cover leasing costs. For a typical Cessna 172, both provide hourly operating rates between $80 and $140, which is significantly less than a flight school rental.

Equity members can recoup their initial capital by selling their share to an incoming pilot, but they remain exposed to aircraft depreciation and must invest the time required to market and sell. Non-equity members own no physical assets, carry zero long-term maintenance liability, and can terminate their membership with minimal notice.
Why Two Clubs Flying The Same Airplane Charge So Differently

Pilot Next's national survey of flying clubs highlights a large gap between individual pricing models. The Hokie Flying Club, which operates out of the Virginia Tech Montgomery Executive Airport, was found to deliver the lowest wet rate. That is, fuel costs are fully included, while maintaining highly accessible monthly dues.

Conversely, the TSS Flying Club in Gaithersburg, Maryland , sits near the top of the pricing spectrum, charging the highest hourly operational rates alongside fixed monthly dues that are several times higher than Hokie. Both clubs function strictly as registered non-profits, thus profit margins cannot account for the pricing discrepancy.

Commercial flight schools charge by a Hobbs meter that tracks actual clock time , but many flying clubs bill using tachometer time, which counts engine revolutions. Tachometers run significantly slower during taxi and low-power operations, delivering notable savings versus traditional rentals. A comprehensive financial comparison must adjust for this variance, as a tachometer-billed hour frequently yields up to 20% more flight time per dollar than the posted rate indicates.

Fleet size, aircraft performance capabilities, and avionics packages explain much of the cost variation. Furthermore, equipment generations skew comparisons, as most clubs operate older legacy airframes while some others invest in modern, high-value Cessna 172S platforms that command higher insurance and debt.

The Virginia Tech records characterize Hokie as a small club running a simple fleet of two aircraft for roughly 35 members. TSS manages four high-performance planes, including a complex, retractable-gear Cessna 182 built for fast cross-country cruising. Still, the primary variable changing real flight costs is the specific meter used to measure time.

In a four-way equity partnership, all fixed costs are divided equally among the co-owners, while each pilot assumes individual responsibility for the direct hourly operating costs of their specific flights. Many models assume each partner logs 50 annual flight hours, with a fleet utilization rate of 200 hours per year. Under this profile, a partner's true operating cost drops to $200 per flight hour, or less than half the expense of sole ownership and comfortably within the price range of flying clubs.
body_zh: 分摊成本：飞行俱乐部和合作伙伴如何使飞机所有权变得负担得起
卢克·迪亚兹 (Luke Diaz) 是一位自由军事作家，拥有在美国海军以及国防和工业工程领域服役的现役经验。他是一名前海军飞行军官，曾在舰载 E-2 鹰眼上执行战术空中控制。
对于任何想要进入通用航空领域的人来说，财务方面通常是进入的首要障碍之一。根据飞行员计划一年飞行的飞行时间，独资或直接租赁远非唯一的飞行途径。对于希望每年在驾驶舱停留 50 小时或更少的休闲飞行员来说，加入飞行俱乐部通常是最好的选择。如果某人的目标是每年飞行 50 到 100 小时，与其他飞行者合作可以提供绝佳的选择。
无论飞机飞行多少距离，机库租金、保险和年检等固定成本都保持不变。这些费用严重惩罚了让飞机闲置的飞行员。因此，共享模式在较低的工作时间门槛下变得更具吸引力，而单独所有权对于高度活跃的乘客来说才开始有意义。俱乐部会员仅在飞机实际运行时支付适度的月费和小时费率。
随着利用率上升到 50 到 100 小时的范围，四方合作伙伴的每小时成本通常会超过飞行俱乐部。一些低成本飞行俱乐部在 70 或 80 小时的纸面上可能看起来仍然更便宜；合作伙伴关系消除了与数十名俱乐部会员竞争周末预订的挫败感。与此同时，即使达到 100 个小时，单独拥有仍然很难证明其合理性。
唯一拥有飞机的固定费用负担沉重，导致飞行节约的飞行员受到重大处罚。共同所有权模式通过改变这些初始费用的分配方式消除了这一财务瓶颈。飞行俱乐部通过每月会费和较低的小时费率将这些固定负债分配给数十名会员，而小型合作伙伴则平均分摊成本。
对典型的价值 100,000 美元的 Cessna 172 的财务估算显示，机库租赁、强制年度检查、Garmin 导航数据库订阅和发动机大修托管的年度固定成本为 16,000 美元。当船东增加 1,700 美元的船体保险和 2,000 美元的年度折旧费时，在考虑发动机每小时运行所需的 100 美元之前，他面临着数千美元的固定义务。
紧急呼叫、等待、航行通告 — 实时信号，无需注册。
当这些固定费用在整个飞行期间摊销时，低使用率下单独拥有的低效率并没有得到改善。每年飞行 25 小时的实际运营成本约为每小时 900 美元。 50 小时时则降至 500 美元，100 小时时则降至更实惠的 300 美元。飞机停飞并不能减轻拥有飞机的基本财务要求，即使飞机从未起飞，账单仍然会产生。
俱乐部通常采用固定月费和可变小时费的定价结构。每月会费旨在支付定期固定费用，例如机库空间、保险和年度机械检查。小时费率用于支付燃料等运营成本。由于这些俱乐部遵循联邦航空管理局第 91 部分的规定，因此它们是仅供会员使用的非营利性私人组织，不能合法向公众出售航班。
股权俱乐部的会员除了每月 100 至 300 美元的会费外，还必须支付 5,000 美元至 30,000 美元以上的买入费才能获得实际所有权份额。另一方面，非股权俱乐部的启动费较低，上限约为 2,000 美元，但每月会费较高，以支付租赁费用。对于典型的塞斯纳 172，两者的每小时运营费都在 80 至 140 美元之间，这比飞行学校的租金要低得多。
股权成员可以通过将其股份出售给即将上任的飞行员来收回初始资本，但他们仍然面临飞机折旧的风险，并且必须投入营销和出售所需的时间。非股权会员不拥有任何实物资产，长期维护责任为零，并且可以在最少通知的情况下终止其会员资格。
为什么乘坐同一架飞机的两个俱乐部收费如此不同
Pilot Next 对飞行俱乐部的全国调查凸显了各个定价模式之间的巨大差距。在弗吉尼亚理工大学蒙哥马利行政机场运营的 Hokie 飞行俱乐部的湿率最低。也就是说，燃料成本完全包含在内，同时保持易于获取的每月会费。
相反，位于马里兰州盖瑟斯堡的 TSS 飞行俱乐部的定价接近顶部，收取最高的每小时运营费率以及比 Hokie 高出数倍的每月固定会费。两个俱乐部都严格按照注册非营利组织运作，因此利润率无法解释定价差异。
商业飞行学校通过跟踪实际时钟时间的霍布斯计收费，但许多飞行俱乐部使用转速计时间计费，转速计时间计算发动机转数。在出租车和低功率运行期间，转速表的运行速度明显减慢，与传统租赁相比，可显着节省成本。必须针对这种差异进行全面的财务比较，因为按转速计计费的小时数通常每美元所产生的飞行时间比公布的费率多出 20%。
机队规模、飞机性能和航空电子设备包解释了大部分成本变化。此外，设备代数的比较也存在偏差，因为大多数俱乐部都使用较旧的传统机身，而另一些俱乐部则投资于现代、高价值的 Cessna 172S 平台，这些平台需要更高的保险和债务。
弗吉尼亚理工大学的记录将 Hokie 描述为一个小型俱乐部，运营着一支由两架飞机组成的简单机队，约有 35 名会员。 TSS 管理着四架高性能飞机，其中包括一架复杂的可伸缩起落架 Cessna 182，专为快速越野巡航而设计。尽管如此，改变实际飞行成本的主要变量是用于测量时间的特定仪表。
在四方股权合作伙伴关系中，所有固定成本在共同所有者之间平均分配，而每个飞行员对其特定航班的直接每小时运营成本承担个人责任。许多模型假设每个合作伙伴每年飞行 50 小时，机队利用率为每年 200 小时。在此模式下，合作伙伴的真实运营成本降至每飞行小时 200 美元，不到单独拥有费用的一半，并且完全在飞行俱乐部的价格范围内。

title_en: Delta Air Lines' Airbus A220 Sits About 50 Seats Below A Boeing 737-800 & 30 Above A Regional Jet
title_zh: 达美航空的空客 A220 座位比波音 737-800 低约 50 个座位，比支线喷气式飞机高 30 个座位
summary: A closer look at how and why the Airbus A220 works for Delta, and why its competitors have stayed away from the jet.
summary_zh: 仔细了解空客 A220 如何以及为何为达美航空服务，以及其竞争对手为何远离这款飞机。
body_en: Delta Air Lines' Airbus A220 Sits About 50 Seats Below A Boeing 737-800 & 30 Above A Regional Jet

Daniel comes to Simple Flying with a business focused approach to the aviation world. Daniel enjoys analyzing strategy and how companies move against each other to gain a step ahead in the skies. Besides strategy, Daniel also has a passion for aircraft design and the history of aviation.

In the US, Delta Air Lines is doing something unique. American Airlines and United Airlines' smallest mainline planes are Airbus A319-100s seating 126-132 passengers, but these airlines are mainly focusing on larger narrowbodies, with the 160 to 172-seat Boeing 737 MAX 8 being their smallest new aircraft.

Delta, on the other hand, is operating new Airbus A220s, including the 109-seat A220-100 (smaller than anything flown by American or United) as well as the 130-seat A220-300 (smaller than anything that its rivals have on order). There are several reasons why Delta ordered the A220, and one of them might be rather unexpected

Meanwhile, flying these planes allows Delta to do some unique things with its network, since it has planes sized almost perfectly between the larger mainline planes and the Delta Connection fleet. These operations also work because, unlike the A319, 737-700, or their re-engined counterparts, the A220 is optimized for this size, which means that they're economical planes to operate.

Delta's order for the A220 is rather infamous for the circumstances surrounding the sale. After Bombardier (the original manufacturer) sold 75 examples of what was then called the CS100 to Delta for well below the sticker price , Boeing filed a dumping petition against Bombardier, which prompted the US Department of Commerce to place a 300% tariff on the CSeries.

As a result, Bombardier partnered with Airbus, then sold off its remaining stake. The aircraft was renamed the A220, and Delta is now the largest customer for the type. Delta flies 45 A220-100s and 47 A220-300s, while it still has 53 A220-300s on order (30 of the 75 A220-100s originally ordered were converted to the larger A220-300, while the airline added another 70 orders).

These planes are mainly based out of New York (at both LaGuardia and JFK), Seattle, Salt Lake City, and Minneapolis, primarily operating longer routes with lower frequency. This is an entirely separate role from the carrier's Boeing 717 fleet, which operates short routes with high frequencies. As is the case at the carrier's rivals, Delta's regional brand is capped at operating 76-seaters.

Meanwhile, Delta's 717s seat 110 passengers, the A319-100s seat 132 passengers, the A320-200s seat 157 passengers, and the 737-800s seat 160 passengers. The A220, but particularly the A220-100, sits in a realm between the larger, more common mainline aircraft and the largest Delta Connection regional jets. This allows for some fairly unique route assignments and network decisions compared to the other two legacies.

While capacity is often used to compare aircraft, the real crucial figures for airlines are operating costs against revenue potential. Compared to the 737-800, the A220 may burn over 20% less fuel per trip, while the type's lower capacity makes it ideal for destinations where Delta may struggle to fill a 737-800. This preserves fare integrity while lowering costs.

The A220-300 burns just slightly more fuel than the A220-100 while seating 21 more passengers and still having transcontinental range, making it the more appealing of the two . Throughout the airline's network, the A220 is widely used for services like Seattle-Washington National, Seattle-Fairbanks, Salt Lake City-Pittsburgh, or JFK-Dallas/Fort Worth.

These are relatively long routes either serving smaller spokes or serving destinations where Delta is a small player, and are only flown once or a handful of times per day. They stretch the economical limits of regional jets: a similarly-sized A319 burns significantly more fuel, while a 737 or A321neo would add significantly more capacity, diluting yields if the same frequency is maintained.

The A220 also operates plenty of routes that don't fit this profile. Services like Salt Lake City-Orange County or LaGuardia-Chicago are short, high-demand, and operated with high frequencies. However, it is the longer, thinner services where the A220 truly shines , and the presence of this aircraft within Delta's fleet allows it to potentially operate these services more effectively than rivals. Of course, operating nonstop flights from Salt Lake City to Pittsburgh isn't the only reason why Delta ordered A220s.

Delta is a very opportunistic buyer, often willing to buy second-hand planes or unusual aircraft types if they're available for low prices. The A220, while an excellent aircraft, also had no commonality with anything else in Delta's fleet when it was first introduced. However, for the price that Bombardier originally sold the planes (allegedly around $20 million each), the planes went from being good to a screaming deal.

The other benefit of the A220 is that it unlocked more 76-seater regional jets. Delta's pilot scope clauses place several restrictions on Delta Connection operations, since contracted regional flying can directly threaten mainline crew jobs . US carriers use 50-seater, 70-seater, and 76-seater aircraft, and the 76-seaters are the most lucrative of the three.

Because of this, Delta's pilot scope clauses place a cap on the number of 76-seaters that may fly under the Delta Connection brand, but this cap may be raised if the airline adds a new small mainline narrowbody type, as it did with the A220. The CSeries/A220 was sold to Delta for a more than reasonable price, and acquiring the type raised the carrier's 76-seater cap to 223 aircraft.

Meanwhile, the aircraft itself is capable and exceptionally fuel-efficient, allowing Delta to more effectively serve long and thin domestic routes while performing well on shorter missions too. Of course, just because the A220 works well for Delta doesn't mean that it works for every US carrier, and it's the only one of the legacy carriers to operate the A220.
Why American & United Don't Fly Small Narrowbodies

The smallest mainline aircraft operated by either American Airlines or United Airlines is the Airbus A319-100, while United also flies the similarly-sized Boeing 737-700. They essentially have the same capacity as the A220-300, but the A319 and 737-700 are much older products that were ordered when the market was significantly different than today. What's more, neither airline operates an aircraft like the A220-100 or 717.

Meanwhile, the smallest modern aircraft that either airline has ordered is the much larger 737 MAX 8. For American, one simple reason why the A220 isn't nearly as appealing is that its pilot scope clauses do not include a 'trigger mechanism' in which a new small narrowbody unlocks additional 76-seaters.
body_zh: 达美航空的空客 A220 座位比波音 737-800 低约 50 个座位，比支线喷气式飞机高 30 个座位
Daniel 带着以商业为中心的方式进入航空界，加入了 Simple Flying。丹尼尔喜欢分析战略以及公司如何相互竞争以取得领先一步。除了战略之外，丹尼尔还对飞机设计和航空历史充满热情。
在美国，达美航空正在做一些独特的事情。美国航空和联合航空最小的干线飞机是空客 A319-100，可容纳 126 至 132 名乘客，但这些航空公司主要专注于较大的窄体飞机，其中 160 至 172 座的波音 737 MAX 8 是他们最小的新飞机。
另一方面，达美航空正在运营新型空客 A220 飞机，包括 109 座的 A220-100（小于美国航空或联合航空运营的任何飞机）以及 130 座的 A220-300（小于其竞争对手订购的任何飞机）。达美航空订购 A220 的原因有几个，其中之一可能相当出人意料
与此同时，驾驶这些飞机使达美航空能够利用其网络做一些独特的事情，因为它的飞机尺寸几乎完美地介于大型干线飞机和达美联运机队之间。这些操作之所以有效，还因为与 A319、737-700 或其重新发动机的同类飞机不同，A220 针对这种尺寸进行了优化，这意味着它们是运行经济的飞机。
达美航空的 A220 订单因销售环境而臭名昭著。庞巴迪（原始制造商）以远低于标价的价格向达美航空出售了 75 架当时称为 CS100 的飞机后，波音公司向庞巴迪提出了倾销申请，促使美国商务部对 C 系列征收 300% 的关税。
结果，庞巴迪与空中客车公司合作，然后出售了剩余的股份。该飞机被更名为 A220，达美航空现在是该机型的最大客户。达美航空执飞 45 架 A220-100 和 47 架 A220-300，但仍有 53 架 A220-300 订单（最初订购的 75 架 A220-100 中的 30 架被改装为更大的 A220-300，同时该航空公司又增加了 70 架订单）。
这些飞机主要以纽约（拉瓜迪亚机场和肯尼迪机场）、西雅图、盐湖城和明尼阿波利斯为基地，主要以较低的频率运营较长的航线。这与该航空公司的波音 717 机队完全不同，该机队运行频率较高的短途航线。与该航空公司竞争对手的情况一样，达美航空的区域品牌运营座位数上限为 76 座。
与此同时，达美航空的717s可容纳110名乘客，A319-100s可容纳132名乘客，A320-200s可容纳157名乘客，737-800s可容纳160名乘客。 A220，尤其是 A220-100，介于更大、更常见的干线飞机和最大的达美联运支线飞机之间。与其他两个遗留系统相比，这允许一些相当独特的路由分配和网络决策。
虽然运力经常被用来比较飞机，但对于航空公司来说，真正关键的数据是运营成本与收入潜力。与 737-800 相比，A220 每次飞行的燃油消耗可能会少 20% 以上，而该机型的载客量较低，使其成为达美航空难以为 737-800 加油的目的地的理想选择。这样可以保持票价完整性，同时降低成本。
A220-300 比 A220-100 燃烧的燃油稍多，同时可多容纳 21 名乘客，并且仍具有横贯大陆的航程，这使其成为两者中更具吸引力的机型。在整个航空公司网络中，A220 广泛用于西雅图-华盛顿国家机场、西雅图-费尔班克斯、盐湖城-匹兹堡或肯尼迪-达拉斯/沃斯堡等航班。
这些航线相对较长，要么服务于较小的辐条，要么服务于达美航空规模较小的目的地，并且每天仅飞行一次或几次。它们突破了支线飞机的经济极限：类似尺寸的 A319 燃烧更多的燃料，而 737 或 A321neo 将显着增加运力，如果保持相同的频率，就会稀释产量。
A220 还运营许多不符合此条件的航线。盐湖城-奥兰治县或拉瓜迪亚-芝加哥等航班时间短、需求高且运营频率高。然而，更长、更薄的服务才是 A220 真正的亮点，达美机队中这架飞机的存在使其能够比竞争对手更有效地运营这些服务。当然，运营从盐湖城飞往匹兹堡的直飞航班并不是达美航空订购 A220 的唯一原因。
达美航空是一个非常机会主义的买家，如果价格低廉，通常愿意购买二手飞机或不寻常的飞机类型。 A220 虽然是一架优秀的飞机，但在首次推出时与达美航空机队中的其他飞机没有任何共同点。然而，以庞巴迪最初出售这些飞机的价格（据称每架约 2000 万美元）来​​看，这些飞机从不错变成了非常划算的交易。
A220 的另一个好处是它解锁了更多 76 座支线飞机。达美航空的飞行员范围条款对达美联运运营施加了多项限制，因为签约的支线飞行可能会直接威胁干线机组人员的工作。美国航空公司使用50座、70座和76座飞机，其中76座是三者中利润最高的。
因此，达美航空的飞行员范围条款对达美联运品牌下的 76 座飞机数量设置了上限，但如果该航空公司增加新的小型干线窄体客机，这一上限可能会提高，就像 A220 那样。 CSeries/A220 以非常合理的价格出售给达美航空，收购该型号后，该航空公司的 76 座飞机数量上限增加到 223 架。
与此同时，飞机本身功能强大且燃油效率极高，使达美航空能够更有效地服务于又长又窄的国内航线，同时在较短的任务中也表现出色。当然，仅仅因为 A220 适用于达美航空并不意味着它适用于所有美国航空公司，并且它是唯一一家运营 A220 的传统航空公司。
为什么美国航空和联合航空不运营小型窄体飞机
美国航空或联合航空运营的最小干线飞机是空客 A319-100，而联合航空还运营类似尺寸的波音 737-700。它们基本上具有与 A220-300 相同的容量，但 A319 和 737-700 是更老的产品，是在市场与当今市场显着不同时订购的。更重要的是，两家航空公司都没有运营 A220-100 或 717 这样的飞机。
与此同时，两家航空公司订购的最小的现代飞机是更大的 737 MAX 8。对于美国航空来说，A220 没有那么有吸引力的一个简单原因是其飞行员范围条款不包括新的小型窄体飞机解锁额外 76 座的“触发机制”。

Her expertise lies in aircraft maintenance, emerging technologies, and advanced air mobility. Lately, Canada's second-largest airline, WestJet , has been making several changes to its US network. Simple Flying recently reported that the carrier had cut services to several major US destinations , including Chicago O'Hare International Airport (ORD), Seattle-Tacoma International Airport (SEA), San Francisco International Airport (SFO), and Boston Logan International Airport (BOS).

However, these are not the only changes to its network. WestJet has also removed flights to the Hawaiian island of Kauai. Notably, the airline has connected the island to Canada for the past 16 years, but the latest cancelation means Kauai will no longer have any nonstop flights to Canada.
WestJet Withdraws From Hawaiian Island Kauai After 16 Years

The Calgary-based airline first started flying to the island in December 2009. It operated seasonal winter flights between Vancouver International Airport (YVR) and Lihue Airport (LIH), using its Boeing 737 MAX 8 and 737-800 aircraft. According to historical schedule data from aviation analytics provider Cirium , WestJet also offered one weekly flight from Calgary International Airport (YYC) during the winter 2021-22 season.

Alas, the airline's service to the Garden Island has now come to an end. The airline operated its last scheduled flight to the island on April 12, 2026, and confirmed that it would not return for the 2026-27 winter season. Nevertheless, it will continue serving three other Hawaiian airports: Ellison Onizuka Kona International Airport (KOA), Daniel K. Inouye International Airport (HNL) in Honolulu, and Kahului Airport (OGG) on Maui.

Orange County Could Be WestJet's Next US Network Cut

The second potential cut, however, has yet to be confirmed. But according to some sources, WestJet could withdraw from Orange County , California, by the end of March 2027, if not sooner. It currently operates two weekly flights between YYC and John Wayne Airport-Orange County Airport (SNA), on Thursdays and Sundays, using its 737 MAX 8 aircraft.

The Canadian airline first entered the Orange County market in 2011, operating flights from both Calgary and Vancouver. The Calgary service was subsequently discontinued in 2012 and returned in 2021 , while flights from Vancouver continued until 2024. If WestJet withdraws completely, Air Canada would be the only airline offering nonstop flights between Orange County and Canada through its daily Vancouver service.

Should WestJet decide to leave, it would be interesting to see how its operating allocation at John Wayne Airport is redistributed. The airport operates under strict capacity restrictions, and airlines are allocated a limited number of average daily departures (ADDs). According to the airport's proposed allocations for 2027 , the Calgary-based airline was assigned approximately 2.3 ADDs.
WestJet Has Scheduled More Than 6,300 US Flights This Winter

For now, it remains to be seen what will happen. Any changes could become clearer in the airline's next schedule update. Nevertheless, the US remains one of WestJet's busiest international markets. For the winter 2026-27 season , the carrier has scheduled around 6,325 flights to the country, offering more than 1 million seats. On its busiest days, the airline will operate more than 50 US-bound flights.

Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport (PHX) is its busiest US destination this winter, accounting for more than 1,000 scheduled flights. In fact, between November 2026 and March 2027, the airline's capacity to Phoenix is up by approximately 27.5% compared with the same period a year earlier. Harry Reid International Airport (LAS) follows as the second-busiest destination, with more than 800 flights scheduled during the season, followed by Palm Springs International Airport (PSP) and Los Angeles International Airport (LAX).

最近，加拿大第二大航空公司西捷航空对其美国网络进行了多项调整。 Simple Flying 最近报道称，该航空公司已削减了飞往美国几个主要目的地的航班，包括芝加哥奥黑尔国际机场 (ORD)、西雅图-塔科马国际机场 (SEA)、旧金山国际机场 (SFO) 和波士顿洛根国际机场 (BOS)。
然而，这些并不是其网络的唯一变化。西捷航空还取消了飞往夏威夷考爱岛的航班。值得注意的是，该航空公司在过去 16 年里一直将可爱岛与加拿大连接起来，但最近的取消意味着可爱岛将不再有任何飞往加拿大的直飞航班。
西捷航空 (WestJet) 退出夏威夷考艾岛 16 年后
这家总部位于卡尔加里的航空公司于 2009 年 12 月首次开通飞往该岛的航班。该公司使用波音 737 MAX 8 和 737-800 飞机运营温哥华国际机场 (YVR) 和利胡埃机场 (LIH) 之间的季节性冬季航班。根据航空分析提供商 Cirium 的历史时刻表数据，西捷航空还在 2021-22 年冬季提供每周一趟从卡尔加里国际机场 (YYC) 出发的航班。
可惜的是，该航空公司飞往花园岛的服务现已结束。该航空公司于 2026 年 4 月 12 日运营了飞往该岛的最后一班定期航班，并确认该航班不会在 2026-27 冬季返回。尽管如此，它将继续为夏威夷的其他三个机场提供服务：檀香山的埃里森·奥尼祖卡·科纳国际机场 (KOA)、丹尼尔·井上国际机场 (HNL) 和毛伊岛的卡胡鲁伊机场 (OGG)。

title_en: Why The Boeing 757 Will Remain As A Narrowbody Icon Once It's Retired
title_zh: 为什么波音 757 退役后仍将成为窄体飞机的标志
summary: Even when its best days are long gone, the Boeing 757 will still be one of the most uniquely capable aircraft to ever exist.
summary_zh: 即使其最好的日子早已过去，波音 757 仍将是有史以来功能最独特的飞机之一。
body_en: Why The Boeing 757 Will Remain As A Narrowbody Icon Once It's Retired
Airline and Airport Management Graduate, Student Commercial Pilot and Commercial Aviation Writer.

The aviation industry has seen few aircraft receive the reverence and operational loyalty of the Boeing 757 . Conceived in the late 1970s to replace the aging trijet Boeing 727 , the twin-engine narrowbody evolved far beyond its original short-haul domestic mandate. It paired an exceptionally clean supercritical wing with overpowered turbofan engines, and with this, Boeing created a high-altitude thoroughbred capable of operating out of restricted city-center airfields that was also capable of crossing vast oceanic expanses.

As major carriers accelerate fleet modernization and phase out aging airframes for modern, high-bypass geared turbofans, the aviation community is losing an icon. The retirement of the 757 is the closing chapter of an engineering era in which raw thrust and structural over-design compensated for fuel efficiency, leaving an unmatched operational coverage across global aviation networks.

The foundational secret behind the 757's legendary performance came from its massive power-to-weight ratio. Boeing equipped the airframe with either the Rolls-Royce RB211-535 or the Pratt & Whitney PW2000, each capable of generating between 36,600 and 43,500 pounds of thrust (162.8 to 193.5 kN). This immense raw power earned the narrowbody the nickname "homesick angel" among flight crews, due to its steep, rocket-like climb gradients immediately after rotation, according to The Aviation Geek Club .

This high-thrust power provided critical operational safety margins when departing from obstacle-constrained or temperature-restricted airfields. At high-elevation destinations or hot-weather airports where standard narrowbodies experience strong engine performance degradation, the 757 maintained its climb capability with full passenger loads. Furthermore, its clean aerodynamic wing design allowed it to cruise efficiently at higher altitudes and faster speeds than typical single-aisle competitors, reducing block times on congested transcontinental and oceanic corridors.

The combination of massive thrust and structural strength enabled the aircraft to handle extreme operational demands that other modern narrowbodies could not handle without offloading cargo or restricting fuel payloads. Still, raw engine power alone didn't define the airframe's commercial success until regulators unlocked its true global reach.

For the first decade of its commercial life, the 757 mainly flew domestic routes across North America and Europe. However, its long-range potential was finally realized in May 1986 when the Federal Aviation Administration approved Rolls-Royce-powered 757s for 120-minute Extended-range Twin-engine Operational Performance Standards, commonly known as ETOPS, as per Aircraft Commerce . It allowed twin-engine narrowbodies to cross large bodies of water, such as the North Atlantic, by ensuring they could fly safely on a single operating engine to an emergency diversion airport within a two-hour window.

By 1990, ETOPS approvals expanded to 180 minutes , enabling airlines to link secondary European cities directly with North American East Coast hubs, meaning that the incredibly high operating costs of widebody quadjets or large twinjets could be avoided. Transatlantic routes from cities like Shannon Airport (SNN), Edinburgh Airport (EDI), and Lisbon Airport (LIS) to New York JFK Airport (JFK) and Boston Logan International Airport (BOS) suddenly became economically viable. Airlines could test new point-to-point international markets with 200 passengers instead of 350, opening new possibilities for global airline network planning.

This regulatory breakthrough laid the groundwork for today's widespread narrowbody transatlantic model and showed that passengers would accept single-aisle aircraft for six-to-seven-hour ocean crossings. ETOPS made the 757 far more enticing to airlines, but the cabin layout was equally useful for operators, contributing heavily to its efficiency on quick turnarounds.

In addition to its engine performance and oceanic range, the 757 featured a distinct structural advantage that modern narrowbodies frequently lack. The L2 door's position immediately forward of the wing root let airlines split passenger boarding flows across two separate cabin entries, as Simple Flying coverage explored . On high-density domestic and charter configurations, ground crews could use both the forward L1 door and the mid-cabin L2 door at the same time, dramatically cutting down aircraft turnaround times at congested hub airports.

The 757's dual-entry capability proved especially valuable for the stretched 757-300 variant, which seated up to 295 passengers in a single-class layout. Without a mid-cabin boarding door, loading nearly three hundred passengers through a single forward door creates severe boarding bottlenecks that extend gate times. The 757's floor plan enabled rapid passenger deplaning and cabin-cleaning cycles, increasing daily aircraft utilization across high-frequency domestic shuttle networks.

Operational efficiencies made the aircraft an indispensable fleet asset for decades, though advancing fuel economics and maintenance realities ultimately shifted airline priorities as the years went by. Furthermore, the very design characteristics that made the airframe exceptional also introduced economic penalties as fuel prices fluctuated, penalties that many airlines refused to take on.

With an unmatched performance envelope, it's hard to see how this aircraft could have fallen out of favor. The 757 eventually succumbed to changing macroeconomic pressures and technological advancements in propulsion, which combined, left the aircraft trailing behind many others. The low-bypass design of the RB211 and PW2000 engines, while delivering immense thrust, burns significantly more fuel per seat-mile than modern turbofans like the Pratt & Whitney GTF or CFM International LEAP-1A . On shorter domestic sectors, the fuel-burn penalty began to eat into profit margins, making older 757s increasingly expensive to operate against newer single-aisle competitors.

Furthermore, aging airframes incur escalating maintenance costs as they pass the thirty-year operational threshold. Heavy structural checks, fuselage skin inspections around high-stress door cutouts, and diminishing availability of proprietary avionics replacement parts require substantial capital investment. Airlines had to decide whether to invest millions in recurring heavy maintenance checks for vintage narrowbodies or redeploy capital toward next-generation aircraft offering double-digit fuel savings. Most airlines chose the latter.
body_zh: 为什么波音 757 退役后仍将成为窄体飞机的标志
航空公司和机场管理毕业生、商业飞行员学生和商业航空作家。
在航空业中，很少有飞机能像波音 757 那样受到尊敬和忠诚度。这款双引擎窄体飞机诞生于 20 世纪 70 年代末，旨在取代老化的三引擎波音 727，其发展远远超出了其最初的短途国内任务。它将异常清洁的超临界机翼与动力强劲的涡轮风扇发动机相结合，由此，波音公司创造了一种高空纯种飞机，能够在受限的市中心机场外运行，也能够穿越广阔的海洋。
随着主要航空公司加速机队现代化并逐步淘汰现代高涵道比齿轮涡轮风扇发动机的老化机身，航空界正在失去一个标志。 757 的退役标志着工程时代的结束篇章，在这个时代，原始推力和结构过度设计弥补了燃油效率，在全球航空网络中留下了无与伦比的运营覆盖范围。
757 传奇性能背后的根本秘密在于其巨大的功率重量比。波音公司为机身配备了劳斯莱斯 RB211-535 或普惠 PW2000，每种发动机都能够产生 36,600 至 43,500 磅的推力（162.8 至 193.5 kN）。根据航空极客俱乐部的说法，这种巨大的原始动力为窄体机赢得了机组人员的绰号“思乡天使”，因为它在旋转后立即出现了陡峭的、火箭般的爬升梯度。
当离开障碍物限制或温度限制的机场时，这种高推力提供了关键的操作安全裕度。在高海拔目的地或炎热天气的机场，标准窄体飞机的发动机性能会严重下降，但 757 仍能在满载乘客的情况下保持爬升能力。此外，其简洁的空气动力学机翼设计使其能够比典型的单通道竞争对手在更高的高度和更快的速度下高效巡航，从而减少在拥挤的横贯大陆和海洋走廊上的阻塞时间。
大推力和结构强度的结合使飞机能够满足其他现代窄体飞机在不卸载货物或限制燃料有效载荷的情况下无法满足的极端操作要求。尽管如此，在监管机构释放其真正的全球影响力之前，仅靠原始发动机功率并不能定义机身的商业成功。
在其商业生涯的前十年，757 主要执飞北美和欧洲的国内航线。然而，它的远程潜力最终在 1986 年 5 月得到实现，当时美国联邦航空管理局批准了由劳斯莱斯提供动力的 757 飞机执行 120 分钟增程双引擎运行性能标准，根据飞机商务部的说法，通常称为 ETOPS。它允许双引擎窄体飞机穿越北大西洋等大片水域，确保它们能够在两小时内通过单引擎安全飞行到紧急改航机场。

到 1990 年，ETOPS 批准时间扩大到 180 分钟，使航空公司能够将欧洲二线城市与北美东海岸枢纽直接连接起来，这意味着可以避免宽体四喷气机或大型双喷气机令人难以置信的高运营成本。从香农机场 (SNN)、爱丁堡机场 (EDI) 和里斯本机场 (LIS) 等城市飞往纽约肯尼迪机场 (JFK) 和波士顿洛根国际机场 (BOS) 的跨大西洋航线突然变得经济可行。航空公司可以用 200 名乘客（而不是 350 名）测试新的点对点国际市场，为全球航空公司网络规划开辟新的可能性。
这一监管突破为当今广泛使用的窄体跨大西洋机型奠定了基础，并表明乘客会接受单通道飞机进行六到七小时的跨洋飞行。 ETOPS 使 757 对航空公司更具吸引力，但机舱布局对运营商同样有用，极大地提高了其快速周转的效率。
除了发动机性能和远洋航程之外，757 还具有现代窄体飞机常常缺乏的独特结构优势。正如《Simple Flying》报道所探索的那样，L2 舱门的位置紧邻机翼根部，让航空公司可以将乘客的登机流程分流到两个独立的机舱入口。在高密度的国内和包机配置中，地勤人员可以同时使用前 L1 舱门和中舱 L2 舱门，从而大大缩短飞机在拥挤的枢纽机场的周转时间。
事实证明，757 的双入口能力对于加长型 757-300 型机型尤其有价值，该机型的单舱布局最多可容纳 295 名乘客。如果没有中舱登机门，通过单个前门装载近 300 名乘客会造成严重的登机瓶颈，从而延长登机时间。 757 的平面图可实现乘客快速下机和客舱清洁周期，从而提高了高频次国内班车网络的每日飞机利用率。
几十年来，运营效率使飞机成为不可或缺的机队资产，尽管随着时间的推移，燃油经济性和维护现实的提高最终改变了航空公司的优先事项。此外，使机身与众不同的设计特征也带来了燃油价格波动带来的经济处罚，而许多航空公司拒绝承担这种处罚。

凭借无与伦比的性能范围，很难看出这架飞机怎么会失宠。 757 最终屈服于不断变化的宏观经济压力和推进技术的进步，这两者结合起来，使该飞机落后于许多其他飞机。 RB211 和 PW2000 发动机的低涵道比设计在提供巨大推力的同时，每座英里燃烧的燃油量比普惠 GTF 或 CFM International LEAP-1A 等现代涡轮风扇发动机要多得多。在较短的国内航线上，燃油消耗开始侵蚀利润率，使得旧型 757 与较新的单通道竞争对手相比运营成本越来越高。
此外，随着老化的机身超过三十年的运行门槛，其维护成本也会不断上升。重型结构检查、高应力舱门切口周围的机身蒙皮检查以及专有航空电子设备更换零件的可用性不断减少，都需要大量的资本投资。航空公司必须决定是投资数百万美元对老式窄体飞机进行定期的重型维护检查，还是将资金重新部署到可节省两位数燃油的下一代飞机上。大多数航空公司选择了后者。

His background spans airport operations, aviation infrastructure, and travel consulting, having worked with global organizations across New Zealand, Europe, and North America.

Combining industry expertise with firsthand travel experience across more than 52 countries and five continents, Aaron covers airlines, airports, aviation policy, and the wider travel sector. He is based in Canterbury, New Zealand.

United Airlines , the world's largest carrier by fleet size, has cut five routes to its Northern neighbor this year. Five nonstop services between US hubs and Canada have been terminated, likely fueled by the ongoing trade war between the two countries. Canadians are hammering down, with their elbows-up movement, opting for Canadian-made goods, and traveling domestically or to other foreign countries.

This has seen demand for trans-border services be subdued , and United is certainly not the only carrier reducing services between the two countries, which otherwise have been close allies. Data from Cirium , an online aviation analytics company, identifies that despite United cancelling five services to Canada, the airline still remains the second-largest airline between the US and Canada, behind Air Canada , but ahead of Delta Air Lines , WestJet and Porter Airlines .
United Airlines Terminates Five Routes To Canada

Washington Dulles International Airport (IAD) saw two routes from its Canadian network terminated this September, as the airline withdrew nonstop services from Dulles to Calgary International Airport (YYC) and Halifax / Stanfield International Airport (YHZ).

Services to the province of Alberta's largest city, Calgary, were operated with a mix of the Boeing 737-800 and 737 MAX 8. United was the only airline connecting the two cities, on a seasonal basis. The airline does not have flights scheduled between the two cities for the 2027 summer season.

Nonstop services to the Canadian Maritimes are also now off the menu, as United withdraws its flight between Dulles and Halifax (YHZ). This route was served up until September, on board the Republic Airways E175 .

United terminated its nonstop service from Chicago O'Hare International Airport (ORD) to Edmonton International Airport (YEG) in September. United was the sole operator on the route, now leaving travelers between the two cities forced to connect via another airport. The airline provided these services onboard the 737-800.

Nonstop flights from Vancouver International Airport (YVR) to Newark Liberty International Airport (EWR) were chopped in October. Operating with a mix of the 737-900 and MAX 9, this route is now operated by Air Canada and JetBlue .

United also cut its nonstop service to Toronto Pearson International Airport (YYZ) from Los Angeles International Airport (LAX) this September. This route was served by the MAX 9, and now leaves Air Canada and Porter Airlines as the sole operators on the route.

title_en: FTC Investigating Airlines Over Personalized Pricing: Don’t Get Too Excited
title_zh: FTC 调查航空公司个性化定价：别太兴奋
summary: The FTC has ordered Delta, United, and JetBlue to hand over data on personalized pricing. Here's why I'm confident the investigation won't amount to much.
summary_zh: 联邦贸易委员会已命令达美航空、美联航和捷蓝航空交出个性化定价数据。这就是为什么我相信调查不会达到目的
body_en: The Federal Trade Commission (FTC) has announced that it’s investigating airlines (among other businesses), to determine to what extent they’re using personalized pricing. I know social media would have us believe that this is the most worthwhile effort ever, but don’t expect anything to come of this.
FTC launches personalized pricing inquiry into airlines

The FTC has just ordered Delta, United, and JetBlue, to provide detailed information that will allow the agency to study the use of personal data to set prices. This investigation also includes pricing and worker compensation for ridesharing and food delivery services, but that’s not what I’ll focus on in this post.

The three airlines must turn over information that will allow the agency to assess whether the pricing for a ticket varies from one person to the next based on factors such as participation in a loyalty program, or analysis of personal data by superintelligence algorithms.

Airlines have 45 days to respond and hand over information, and it’s noted how under Section 6(b) of the FTC Act, the commission has the authority to conduct wide-ranging studies that do not have a specific law enforcement purpose.
Here’s how FTC Chairman Andrew Ferguson describes this

“We intend to scrutinize the opaque methodology that some companies in these industries may be using to determine how much consumers pay or how much gig workers are paid for the same product or service. Consumers deserve to know whether companies use their web surfing habits or other personal data to estimate the highest price they can charge each consumer. Workers also deserve to know if their compensation is affected by how companies use their personal data.”
This airline investigation is unlikely to prove fruitful

The general public largely hates airlines, and thinks they’re trying to rip people off. I have a different take — while there are aspects of the industry that frustrate me, it’s a really tough, low margin industry, and people don’t realize how expensive flights are to operate. The people most frequently getting screwed by airlines are the investors. 😉

The thing is, airline pricing is no doubt incredibly complex, and the goal is to maximize revenue with each passenger as much as possible. However, that doesn’t mean we’re actually seeing any sort of personalized pricing.

We have seen an increase in accusations of this in recent times, with all kinds of viral social media posts, of people claiming airlines are trying to charge two people different prices at the same time. In just about example I’ve seen, there has been a logical explanation, and it had nothing to do with the IP address or loyalty program participation.

Admittedly the fact that we live in an AI era, and Delta executives have made some pretty dumb comments along these lines, haven’t helped. I am a little confused why only three US carriers are being investigated, though. How were they chosen, exactly?

There’s nothing wrong with the FTC trying to investigate this, though I’m willing to say with a very high level of certainty that nothing will come of this. Actual personalized pricing among the major US carriers in the way that’s being suggested simply isn’t happening. Period.

How do I know? Well, for one, I have a generally good understanding of how airline pricing works. Complex as it is, there is a method to the madness. I’ve also yet to see an actual example of that in a defensible way. I also have quite a few friends who work in pricing at airlines, and they confirm the same (and these are people who tell me the truth off the record, even if it doesn’t fit their preferred narrative).

I will say, I think investigating rideshare and food delivery compensation is a fair initiative, and I think services like Uber should probably be pretty worried there. Or at least I saw the below video recently, and that definitely made me think that something was up. Then again, it’s not something I fully understand, so maybe I’m being as foolish here as people are in their beliefs about airlines… I don’t know!

The FTC is investigating airlines, to determine if they’re using personalized pricing on consumers. There’s nothing wrong with looking into this, but I’ll just say up front that I’m very confident nothing will come of this. Airlines no doubt have very complex pricing, but that doesn’t mean that they’re charging people different prices based on their IP, their loyalty program participation, etc.
Looking into rideshare and food delivery driver compensation does seem like a more worthwhile endeavor, and I feel like there might actually be some things to learn there…
What do you make of the FTC investigating airlines?
body_zh: 美国联邦贸易委员会 (FTC) 宣布正在调查航空公司（以及其他企业），以确定他们在多大程度上使用个性化定价。我知道社交媒体会让我们相信这是有史以来最有价值的努力，但不要指望这会产生任何结果。
FTC 对航空公司发起个性化定价调查

这三家航空公司必须交出信息，使该机构能够根据参与忠诚度计划或通过超级智能算法分析个人数据等因素来评估机票价格是否因人而异。

FTC 主席安德鲁·弗格森 (Andrew Ferguson) 是这样描述的
“我们打算仔细审查这些行业中的一些公司可能使用的不透明方法，以确定消费者为相同的产品或服务支付多少费用或零工工资。消费者应该知道公司是否使用他们的网上冲浪习惯或其他个人数据来估计他们可以向每个消费者收取的最高价格。工人也应该知道他们的薪酬是否受到公司如何使用其个人数据的影响。”

事实是，航空公司的定价无疑极其复杂，其目标是尽可能最大化每位乘客的收入。然而，这并不意味着我们实际上看到了任何形式的个性化定价。
近年来，我们看到越来越多的人指责航空公司试图同时向两个人收取不同的价格，各种社交媒体帖子在社交媒体上疯传。在我见过的例子中，有一个合乎逻辑的解释，它与 IP 地址或忠诚度计划参与无关。
诚然，我们生活在人工智能时代，而达美航空的高管在这些方面发表了一些相当愚蠢的评论，但这并没有帮助。不过，我有点困惑为什么只有三家美国运营商受到调查。他们到底是如何被选中的？
联邦贸易委员会试图调查此事并没有什么问题，尽管我愿意非常肯定地说这不会有任何结果。美国主要运营商所建议的实际个性化定价根本没有发生。时期。
我怎么知道？嗯，一方面，我对航空公司定价的运作方式总体上有很好的了解。尽管它很复杂，但有一种方法可以达到疯狂。我还没有看到一个可以辩护的实际例子。我还有很多在航空公司从事定价工作的朋友，他们也证实了这一点（这些人私下告诉我真相，即使这不符合他们喜欢的叙述）。
我想说的是，我认为调查拼车和送餐补偿是一项公平的举措，我认为像 Uber 这样的服务可能应该对此感到非常担心。或者至少我最近看到了下面的视频，这肯定让我觉得出了什么问题。话又说回来，这不是我完全理解的事情，所以也许我在这里就像人们对航空公司的信念一样愚蠢……我不知道！

title_en: The Aging Narrowbody US Airlines Don't Want A Direct Replacement For In 2026
title_zh: 美国航空公司不希望在 2026 年直接更换老化的窄体飞机
summary: The A320-200 is going away, and the A320neo is not selling well in the US.
summary_zh: A320-200 即将退出市场，而 A320neo 在美国的销量也不佳。
body_en: The Aging Narrowbody US Airlines Don't Want A Direct Replacement For In 2026

Daniel comes to Simple Flying with a business focused approach to the aviation world. Daniel enjoys analyzing strategy and how companies move against each other to gain a step ahead in the skies. Besides strategy, Daniel also has a passion for aircraft design and the history of aviation.

The Airbus A320 family is the most successful commercial jet airliner program of all time, having received over 20,000 orders while nearly 13,000 have been delivered. US airlines are among the largest customers for the type, and there are currently seven airlines operating over 1,500 A320 family aircraft in the country.

However, while the A320 family is generally popular with American carriers, there is one variant that the country's airlines are moving away from, and that is the original A320, flown by six US carriers. The very first A320s were designated as A320-100s, but very few of these were produced, as Airbus quickly rolled out the improved A320-200, which was operated in large numbers by US carriers.

However, some US airlines have started to phase out their A320-200 fleets, even while keeping their A319-100s and 737s. What's more, only one US airline, Frontier, is operating the A320neo, the direct successor to the A320-200, and there's no indication that any other carrier is planning to buy A320neos.

JetBlue, Frontier, and Allegiant Air are all low-cost carriers operating large A320 fleets, and most of their planes were acquired new or lightly used (much of Allegiant's fleet was purchased second-hand, but these planes still aren't particularly old). The A320s that these three airlines have retired were mainly their oldest examples, which makes sense as low-cost carriers tend to use their planes fairly heavily.

More interesting, however, are the Airbus fleets operated by the three legacy carriers. Northwest Airlines was the US launch customer for the A320, and it took its first A320-200 in 1989. The airline also ordered the A319-100, and it accumulated a total of 77 A319-100s along with 78 A320-200s, although some examples were removed during financial difficulties in the 2000s.

When Delta merged with Northwest in 2008, it inherited 57 A319-100s and 69 A320-200s, and it has since removed 29 A320-200s. United Airlines took delivery of its first A320-200 in 1993, and it ordered a total of 98 examples (one of which was scrapped in 2003) from Airbus, while it also accumulated 55 A319-100s. The airline later purchased 28 second-hand A319-100s to its operating fleet, while it retired 14 A319-100s in recent years.

Meanwhile, United added two second-hand A320-200s in 2017, while it retired 35 A320-200s more recently. Note that United also purchased additional A319-100s and A320-200s for parts, and these planes never entered service. US Airways took its first A320-200 in 1999, its first A319-100 in 1998, and its first A321-200 in 2001.

American Airlines also made its own A320 family order in 2011, and after the merger was done and all orders were finished, American ended up with 133 A319-100s, 68 A320-200s, as well as 219 A321-200s. One A319-100 has been stored, and one A321-200 was written off, while American has removed 20 A320-200s.

The A320 is still thought of as a modern airliner, given its technological innovations and the fact that it's still in production as the A320neo, which has few changes apart from the engines. It is, however, the second-oldest commercial aircraft type still on sale as a passenger airliner (behind only the Boeing 737 ), while Northwest and United in particular were early customers for the type.

United and Delta are actively retiring A320-200s because these aircraft are among the oldest in their fleets, with some of them exceeding 30 years old. US carriers tend to operate their planes for about 25 to 30 years in general, and these planes are simply reaching the end of their economic lives.

For the most part, US carriers aren't retiring A319-100s or 737s because these aircraft are much younger than the A320-200s being flown by Delta and United, as both types started arriving in the late 1990s. American Airlines is the best proof of this: it removed 20 relatively young A320-200s in the 2010s as it was upgauging to new A321-200s and had a large order for the type.

However, it hasn't retired any examples since because its A320-200s are younger than those flown by United and Delta. Eventually, its A320-200s will leave the fleet, but American is even refurbishing the interiors of these aircraft in the meantime to keep them flying until the 2030s. Meanwhile, Delta and United are actively retiring their A320-200s due to their advanced age.

The only two airlines to take A320neos were Frontier and Spirit Airlines (which has since gone out of business), while none of the three legacy carriers have. These airlines still operate a significant number of A320-200s and have also ordered hundreds of A321neos. The A320 family remains highly popular with US airlines, but just not the A320neo, even as airlines worldwide have ordered over 4,000 examples.

Ultimately, this is because today, the legacy carriers are upgauging.The Airbus A321neo burns only slightly more fuel than the A320neo, while carrying significantly more passengers. In addition, the A321neo has essentially enough range for any US airline's needs, so flying the A320neo essentially leaves money on the table.

The US legacy carriers in particular also heavily employ price segmentation in their business strategies, and this reduces the need to operate smaller aircraft on routes with less demand. As such, these airlines are increasingly standardizing on large narrowbodies. On the Boeing side, US airlines have collectively ordered hundreds of 737 MAX 10s in addition to their A321neos, as the aircraft essentially serves the same role.

United and Alaska Airlines have also ordered a substantial number of 737 MAX 9s, which is Boeing's largest narrowbody that it's currently delivering. Southwest has ordered 500 MAX 8s, but it generally favors smaller aircraft. Meanwhile, the legacy carriers have ordered fewer 737 MAX 8s than MAX 10s, with Delta not ordering any at all.

While the US legacy airlines are generally standardizing on large narrowbodies, there remains a place within their fleets for smaller aircraft to serve low-demand routes and challenging airfields. For this role, it's the A320neo and 737 MAX 8 that have emerged as the most popular choices, but in the US, the 737 MAX 8 has become favored.

Notably, American and United, which are both major Airbus operators, have ordered over 100 737 MAX 8s each, but no A320neos . As a modernized version of the successful A320-200, the A320neo is a perfectly capable and efficient aircraft, which is why it remains popular globally. However, the 737 MAX 8 is slightly larger, burns about the same amount of fuel, has slightly more range, and has slightly better climb performance.
body_zh: 美国航空公司不希望在 2026 年直接更换老化的窄体飞机
Daniel 带着以商业为中心的方式进入航空界，加入了 Simple Flying。丹尼尔喜欢分析战略以及公司如何相互竞争以取得领先一步。除了战略之外，丹尼尔还对飞机设计和航空历史充满热情。
空客 A320 系列是有史以来最成功的商用喷气式客机项目，已收到超过 20,000 份订单，近 13,000 架已交付。美国航空公司是该机型的最大客户之一，目前有 7 家航空公司在该国运营超过 1,500 架 A320 系列飞机。
然而，虽然 A320 系列飞机普遍受到美国航空公司的欢迎，但该国的航空公司正在放弃一种型号，那就是最初的 A320，由六家美国航空公司运营。第一批 A320 被指定为 A320-100，但产量很少，因为空中客车公司很快推出了改进的 A320-200，并由美国航空公司大量运营。
然而，一些美国航空公司已开始逐步淘汰其 A320-200 机队，同时保留 A319-100 和 737 飞机。更重要的是，只有一家美国航空公司 Frontier 正在运营 A320neo，它是 A320-200 的直接后继机型，没有迹象表明任何其他航空公司计划购买 A320neo。
捷蓝航空、边疆航空和忠诚航空都是运营着大型 A320 机队的低成本航空公司，它们的大部分飞机都是新购置的或轻度使用的（忠诚航空的大部分机队是二手购买的，但这些飞机仍然不是特别旧）。这三家航空公司退役的 A320 飞机主要是最古老的机型，这是有道理的，因为低成本航空公司往往会大量使用他们的飞机。
然而，更有趣的是由三大传统航空公司运营的空客机队。西北航空公司是 A320 的美国启动客户，于 1989 年接收了第一架 A320-200。该航空公司还订购了 A319-100，并且累计购买了 77 架 A319-100 和 78 架 A320-200，尽管在 2000 年代的财务困难期间取消了一些飞机。

2008 年达美航空与西北航空合并时，继承了 57 架 A319-100 和 69 架 A320-200，并删除了 29 架 A320-200。联合航空于1993年接收了第一架A320-200，并向空中客车公司总共订购了98架（其中一架于2003年报废），同时还积累了55架A319-100。该航空公司随后为其运营机队购买了 28 架二手 A319-100 飞机，并在近年来退役了 14 架 A319-100 飞机。
与此同时，美联航在 2017 年增加了两架二手 A320-200 飞机，最近又退役了 35 架 A320-200 飞机。请注意，美联航还额外购买了 A319-100 和 A320-200 的零部件，但这些飞机从未投入使用。全美航空于 1999 年接收第一架 A320-200，于 1998 年接收第一架 A319-100，于 2001 年接收第一架 A321-200。
美国航空也在2011年订购了自己的A320系列飞机，合并完成并完成所有订单后，美国航空最终拥有133架A319-100、68架A320-200和219架A321-200。一架 A319-100 已被储存，一架 A321-200 被注销，而美国航空已拆除 20 架 A320-200。
鉴于 A320 的技术创新以及它仍在生产中的 A320neo（除了发动机之外几乎没有变化）这一事实，A320 仍然被认为是一款现代客机。然而，它是仍在作为客机销售的第二古老的商用飞机类型（仅次于波音 737），而西北航空和联合航空尤其是该型号的早期客户。
美联航和达美航空正在积极退役 A320-200 飞机，因为这些飞机是其机队中最古老的飞机之一，其中一些飞机的机龄已超过 30 年。美国航空公司的飞机一般运营时间约为 25 至 30 年，而这些飞机的经济寿命即将结束。
大多数情况下，美国航空公司不会退役 A319-100 或 737 飞机，因为这些飞机比达美航空和联合航空运营的 A320-200 飞机要年轻得多，因为这两种类型的飞机都是在 90 年代末开始抵达的。美国航空就是最好的证明：它在 2010 年代淘汰了 20 架相对较新的 A320-200，因为它正在升级为新的 A321-200，并获得了该型号的大量订单。
然而，此后它没有退役任何飞机，因为它的 A320-200 飞机比联合航空和达美航空运营的飞机更年轻。最终，其 A320-200 飞机将退出机队，但美国航空甚至同时翻新这些飞机的内饰，以保证它们能够飞行到 2030 年代。与此同时，达美航空和美联航由于 A320-200 机龄较高，正在积极退役。

仅有两家采用 A320neo 的航空公司是边疆航空公司 (Frontier Airlines) 和精神航空公司 (Spirit Airlines)（该航空公司现已停业），而这三家传统航空公司均没有采用 A320neo。这些航空公司仍然运营着大量的 A320-200 飞机，并且还订购了数百架 A321neo 飞机。 A320 系列仍然深受美国航空公司的欢迎，但 A320neo 却不受欢迎，尽管全球航空公司已订购了 4,000 多架。
归根结底，这是因为如今传统航空公司正在不断升级。空客 A321neo 的燃油消耗仅比 A320neo 稍多一点，但载客量却明显增加。此外，A321neo 的航程基本上足以满足任何美国航空公司的需求，因此乘坐 A320neo 基本上可以省钱。
特别是美国传统航空公司还在其业务战略中大量采用价格细分，这减少了在需求较少的航线上运营小型飞机的需要。因此，这些航空公司越来越多地对大型窄体飞机进行标准化。在波音方面，除了 A321neo 之外，美国航空公司还集体订购了数百架 737 MAX 10，因为这些飞机本质上发挥着相同的作用。
美联航和阿拉斯加航空也订购了大量 737 MAX 9，这是波音目前交付的最大窄体飞机。西南航空已订购 500 架 MAX 8，但总体上更青睐小型飞机。与此同时，传统航空公司订购的 737 MAX 8 数量少于 MAX 10，达美航空根本没有订购任何飞机。
虽然美国传统航空公司普遍对大型窄体飞机进行标准化，但其机队中仍然有小型飞机的一席之地，以服务低需求航线和具有挑战性的机场。对于这一角色，A320neo 和 737 MAX 8 成为最受欢迎的选择，但在美国，737 MAX 8 受到青睐。
值得注意的是，美国航空和联合航空这两家空客主要运营商均已订购了超过 100 架 737 MAX 8，但没有订购 A320neo。作为成功的 A320-200 的现代化版本，A320neo 是一款性能完美且高效的飞机，这就是它在全球仍然受欢迎的原因。然而，737 MAX 8 稍大一些，燃烧的燃油量大致相同，航程略长，爬升性能稍好。

Texan carrier Avelo Airlines has drastically reduced its network from Wilmington International Airport (ILM), North Carolina, readjusting its network down to just a handful of nonstop destinations. The carrier dropped a total of eight routes in January, with one more terminated this August.

Data from Cirium , an online aviation analytics company, shows Avelo's dramatic drop from the fourth busiest airport in the airlines network, to now 12th. This November, Wilmington will see a total of 11 weekly departures, down from 27 this time last year.

Avelo is an ultra-low-cost carrier that was initially founded in 1987 as Casino Express Airlines . This changed to Xtra Airways in 2025 before becoming Avelo in 2021. The airline, under its new branding, had its first scheduled flight in April 2021 from Hollywood Burbank Airport (BUR) to Sonoma County (STS).

The carrier has rapidly expanded its network, focusing on affordable convenience for travelers, and operates point-to-point flights between secondary underserved airports. This avoids major airports with high landing fees and sees the airline primarily operate alone, instead of head-to-head with other major carriers.
